passages.text: O foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you? Before your very eyes Jesus Christ was clearly portrayed as crucified.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the Galatians.
He calls them foolish.
He asks, “Who has bewitched you?”
He reminds them of Jesus Christ.
He says Jesus Christ was clearly shown to them as crucified.
They saw this with their own eyes.
passages.original: Ὦ ἀνόητοι Γαλάται τίς ὑμᾶς ἐβάσκανεν οἷς κατ’ ὀφθαλμοὺς Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς προεγράφη ἐσταυρωμένος

passages.text: I would like to learn just one thing from you: Did you receive the Spirit by works of the law, or by hearing with faith?
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the Galatians.
Paul asks a clear question.
Paul wants to know one thing from them.
He asks, “Did you receive the Spirit by doing works of the law?”
He also asks, “Or did you receive the Spirit by hearing with faith?”
passages.original: τοῦτο μόνον θέλω μαθεῖν ἀφ’ ὑμῶν ἐξ ἔργων νόμου τὸ Πνεῦμα ἐλάβετε ἢ ἐξ ἀκοῆς πίστεως

passages.text: Are you so foolish? After starting in the Spirit, are you now finishing in the flesh?
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the Galatians.
He calls them foolish.
They began their Christian life by the Spirit.
Now they try to finish by human effort.
They started with God’s Spirit.
Now they rely on their own flesh.
passages.original: Οὕτως ἀνόητοί ἐστε ἐναρξάμενοι Πνεύματι νῦν σαρκὶ ἐπιτελεῖσθε

passages.text: Have you suffered so much for nothing, if it really was for nothing?
passages.sermon: You have suffered many things.\r\nYou may have suffered for no reason.\r\nI ask if your suffering truly was for nothing.
passages.original: τοσαῦτα ἐπάθετε εἰκῇ εἴ γε καὶ εἰκῇ

passages.text: Does God lavish His Spirit on you and work miracles among you because you practice the law, or because you hear and believe?
passages.sermon:
God gives you His Spirit.
God works miracles among you.
God does not do this because you practice the law.
God does this because you hear and believe.
passages.original: ὁ οὖν ἐπιχορηγῶν ὑμῖν τὸ Πνεῦμα καὶ ἐνεργῶν δυνάμεις ἐν ὑμῖν ἐξ ἔργων νόμου ἢ ἐξ ἀκοῆς πίστεως

passages.text: So also, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”
passages.sermon: Abraham was a man who believed God.\r\nGod saw Abraham’s faith.\r\nGod counted Abraham’s faith as righteousness.
passages.original: Καθὼς Ἀβραὰμ ἐπίστευσεν τῷ Θεῷ καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην

passages.text: Understand, then, that those who have faith are sons of Abraham.
passages.sermon: Those who have faith are sons of Abraham.\r\nFaith makes people sons of Abraham.\r\nUnderstand this truth.
passages.original: Γινώσκετε ἄρα ὅτι οἱ ἐκ πίστεως οὗτοι υἱοί εἰσιν Ἀβραάμ

passages.text: The Scripture foresaw that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, and foretold the gospel to Abraham: “All nations will be blessed through you.”
passages.sermon:
The Scripture saw something in advance.
The Scripture saw that God would justify the Gentiles by faith.
God would declare the Gentiles righteous because of their faith.
The Scripture announced this good news to Abraham before it happened.
God said to Abraham, “All nations will be blessed through you.”
passages.original: προϊδοῦσα δὲ ἡ γραφὴ ὅτι ἐκ πίστεως δικαιοῖ τὰ ἔθνη ὁ Θεὸς προευηγγελίσατο τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ὅτι Ἐνευλογηθήσονται ἐν σοὶ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη

passages.text: So those who have faith are blessed along with Abraham, the man of faith.
passages.sermon:
Those who have faith receive a blessing.
Abraham was a man of faith.
God blessed Abraham because of his faith.
God blesses all who have faith, just as He blessed Abraham.
passages.original: ὥστε οἱ ἐκ πίστεως εὐλογοῦνται σὺν τῷ πιστῷ Ἀβραάμ

passages.text: All who rely on works of the law are under a curse. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who does not continue to do everything written in the Book of the Law.”
passages.sermon: All people who depend on works of the law are under a curse.\r\nThe law means the commands God gave in the Book of the Law.\r\nGod says in the Scriptures, “Cursed is everyone who does not keep doing everything written in the Book of the Law.”
passages.original: Ὅσοι γὰρ ἐξ ἔργων νόμου εἰσὶν ὑπὸ κατάραν εἰσίν γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι Ἐπικατάρατος πᾶς ὃς οὐκ ἐμμένει πᾶσιν τοῖς γεγραμμένοις ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τοῦ νόμου τοῦ ποιῆσαι αὐτά

passages.text: Now it is clear that no one is justified before God by the law, because, “The righteous will live by faith.”
passages.sermon:
No one becomes righteous before God by following the law.
God does not justify anyone through the law.
This fact is clear.
Scripture says, “The righteous will live by faith.”
God gives life to the righteous through faith.
Faith, not the law, brings justification before God.
passages.original: ὅτι δὲ ἐν νόμῳ οὐδεὶς δικαιοῦται παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ δῆλον ὅτι Ὁ δίκαιος ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται

passages.text: The law, however, is not based on faith; on the contrary, “The man who does these things will live by them.”
passages.sermon:
The law does not come from faith.
The law is not based on faith.
The law requires actions.
A person must do the things written in the law.
If a person does these things, he will live by them.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ νόμος οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ πίστεως ἀλλ’ Ὁ ποιήσας αὐτὰ ζήσεται ἐν αὐτοῖς

passages.text: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a tree.”
passages.sermon:
Christ redeemed us.
He redeemed us from the curse of the law.
He became a curse for us.
The law brings a curse.
Christ took that curse upon himself.
Scripture says, “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a tree.”
Christ was hung on a tree.
He fulfilled what was written.
He took our place under the curse.
passages.original: Χριστὸς ἡμᾶς ἐξηγόρασεν ἐκ τῆς κατάρας τοῦ νόμου γενόμενος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν κατάρα ὅτι γέγραπται Ἐπικατάρατος πᾶς ὁ κρεμάμενος ἐπὶ ξύλου

passages.text: He redeemed us in order that the blessing promised to Abraham would come to the Gentiles in Christ Jesus, so that by faith we might receive the promise of the Spirit.
passages.sermon:
Christ redeemed us.
He did this for a purpose.
God promised Abraham a blessing.
This blessing would come to the Gentiles.
The blessing comes through Jesus Christ.
God wants us to receive the promise of the Spirit.
We receive this promise by faith.
passages.original: ἵνα εἰς τὰ ἔθνη ἡ εὐλογία τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ γένηται ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ ἵνα τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ Πνεύματος λάβωμεν διὰ τῆς πίστεως

passages.text: Brothers, let me put this in human terms. Even a human covenant, once it is ratified, cannot be canceled or amended.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to fellow believers.
Paul calls them brothers.
Paul explains his point using a human example.
A covenant is an agreement between people.
When people make a covenant and confirm it, it becomes binding.
No one can cancel a confirmed human covenant.
No one can add to a confirmed human covenant.
passages.original: Ἀδελφοί κατὰ ἄνθρωπον λέγω ὅμως ἀνθρώπου κεκυρωμένην διαθήκην οὐδεὶς ἀθετεῖ ἢ ἐπιδιατάσσεται

passages.text: The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. The Scripture does not say, “and to seeds,” meaning many, but “and to your seed,” meaning One, who is Christ.
passages.sermon:
God spoke promises to Abraham.
God also spoke these promises to Abraham’s seed.
The Scripture does not say, “and to seeds.”
“Seeds” would mean many descendants.
Instead, the Scripture says, “and to your seed.”
“Seed” means one descendant.
This one descendant is Christ.
passages.original: τῷ δὲ Ἀβραὰμ ἐρρέθησαν αἱ ἐπαγγελίαι καὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ οὐ λέγει Καὶ τοῖς σπέρμασιν ὡς ἐπὶ πολλῶν ἀλλ’ ὡς ἐφ’ ἑνός Καὶ τῷ σπέρματί σου ὅς ἐστιν Χριστός

passages.text: What I mean is this: The law that came 430 years later does not revoke the covenant previously established by God, so as to nullify the promise.
passages.sermon:
God made a covenant with Abraham.
God established this covenant before the law existed.
The law came 430 years after God made this covenant.
The law does not cancel God’s covenant.
The law does not make God’s promise void.
passages.original: Τοῦτο δὲ λέγω διαθήκην προκεκυρωμένην ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ ὁ μετὰ τετρακόσια καὶ τριάκοντα ἔτη γεγονὼς νόμος οὐκ ἀκυροῖ εἰς τὸ καταργῆσαι τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν

passages.text: For if the inheritance depends on the law, then it no longer depends on a promise; but God freely granted it to Abraham through a promise.
passages.sermon:
God gave Abraham a promise.
God freely granted Abraham an inheritance through this promise.
If the inheritance depends on the law, it does not depend on a promise.
But God did not give the inheritance through the law.
God gave the inheritance to Abraham by a promise.
passages.original: εἰ γὰρ ἐκ νόμου ἡ κληρονομία οὐκέτι ἐξ ἐπαγγελίας τῷ δὲ Ἀβραὰμ δι’ ἐπαγγελίας κεχάρισται ὁ Θεός

passages.text: Why then was the law given? It was added because of transgressions, until the arrival of the seed to whom the promise referred. It was administered through angels by a mediator.
passages.sermon:
God gave the law for a reason.
People sinned.
God added the law because of these sins.
The law was meant to last for a time.
It would last until the promised descendant arrived.
God made this promise about the descendant earlier.
Angels gave the law.
A mediator helped give the law.
passages.original: Τί οὖν ὁ νόμος τῶν παραβάσεων χάριν προσετέθη ἄχρις οὗ ἔλθῃ τὸ σπέρμα ᾧ ἐπήγγελται διαταγεὶς δι’ ἀγγέλων ἐν χειρὶ μεσίτου

passages.text: A mediator is unnecessary, however, for only one party; but God is one.
passages.sermon: A mediator is not needed when there is only one party.\r\nGod is one.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ μεσίτης ἑνὸς οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ δὲ Θεὸς εἷς ἐστιν

passages.text: Is the law, then, opposed to the promises of God? Certainly not! For if a law had been given that could impart life, then righteousness would certainly have come from the law.
passages.sermon:
God made promises.
\r\nThe law does not oppose God’s promises.
\r\nThe law and God’s promises do not conflict.
\r\nNo law can give life.
\r\nIf a law could give life, then righteousness would come from the law.
\r\nBut righteousness does not come from the law.
passages.original: Ὁ οὖν νόμος κατὰ τῶν ἐπαγγελιῶν τοῦ Θεοῦ μὴ γένοιτο εἰ γὰρ ἐδόθη νόμος ὁ δυνάμενος ζωοποιῆσαι ὄντως ἐκ νόμου ἂν ἦν ἡ δικαιοσύνη

passages.text: But the Scripture pronounces all things confined by sin, so that by faith in Jesus Christ the promise might be given to those who believe.
passages.sermon:
Scripture speaks with authority.
Scripture declares that sin confines everything.
Sin holds all people and all things captive.
God gives a promise.
God gives this promise through faith in Jesus Christ.
God gives this promise to everyone who believes.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ συνέκλεισεν ἡ γραφὴ τὰ πάντα ὑπὸ ἁμαρτίαν ἵνα ἡ ἐπαγγελία ἐκ πίστεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ δοθῇ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν

passages.text: Before this faith came, we were held in custody under the law, locked up until faith should be revealed.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote to the Galatians about the law and faith in Jesus Christ.
Before faith in Jesus Christ came, we lived under the law.
The law kept us in custody.
The law locked us up.
We waited for faith to be revealed.
passages.original: Πρὸ τοῦ δὲ ἐλθεῖν τὴν πίστιν ὑπὸ νόμον ἐφρουρούμεθα συνκλειόμενοι εἰς τὴν μέλλουσαν πίστιν ἀποκαλυφθῆναι

passages.text: So the law became our guardian to lead us to Christ, that we might be justified by faith.
passages.sermon: The law acted as our guardian.\r\nThe law guided us toward Christ.\r\nThe law did this so that we could be justified by faith.
passages.original: ὥστε ὁ νόμος παιδαγωγὸς ἡμῶν γέγονεν εἰς Χριστόν ἵνα ἐκ πίστεως δικαιωθῶμεν

passages.text: Now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian.
passages.sermon:
Faith has now come.
We are not under a guardian anymore.
Faith in Christ Jesus has arrived.
The law was our guardian before faith came.
Now, faith has replaced the law as our guide.
We do not need the law as a guardian now.
We live by faith in Christ.
passages.original: ἐλθούσης δὲ τῆς πίστεως οὐκέτι ὑπὸ παιδαγωγόν ἐσμεν

passages.text: You are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus.
passages.sermon:
You have faith in Christ Jesus.
This faith makes you children of God.
All of you who believe in Christ are sons of God.
Faith in Jesus Christ gives you this new identity.
You are now part of God's family because of your faith in Christ.
passages.original: Πάντες γὰρ υἱοὶ Θεοῦ ἐστε διὰ τῆς πίστεως ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: For all of you who were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.
passages.sermon: All of you who were baptized into Christ have put on Christ.\r\nYou have clothed yourselves with Christ.
passages.original: ὅσοι γὰρ εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε Χριστὸν ἐνεδύσασθε

passages.text: There is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote to Christians in Galatia.
He spoke to people who believed in Jesus Christ.
He said, “You are all one in Christ Jesus.”
In Christ, God does not separate people by race.
There is no Jew.
There is no Greek.
God does not separate people by social status.
There is no slave.
There is no free person.
God does not separate people by gender.
There is no male.
There is no female.
All believers are united in Christ Jesus.
passages.original: οὐκ ἔνι Ἰουδαῖος οὐδὲ Ἕλλην οὐκ ἔνι δοῦλος οὐδὲ ἐλεύθερος οὐκ ἔνι ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ πάντες γὰρ ὑμεῖς εἷς ἐστε ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham’s seed and heirs according to the promise.
passages.sermon:
If you belong to Christ, this is true.
You are Abraham’s seed.
You are heirs.
You receive this by God’s promise.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ ὑμεῖς Χριστοῦ ἄρα τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ σπέρμα ἐστέ κατ’ ἐπαγγελίαν κληρονόμοι
